comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C59, C60, C73 regarding the final evolved sequence composition and combined rescue effects. Both evaluations accept the experimental findings without challenge.

Perfect agreement on claims C30, C33 regarding functional intermediates and validity of tissue culture assays. Both accept that intermediates showed activity and that the assay system appropriately represents intracellular NP function.

Disagreement on claims C16, C17, C24, C25 regarding the stability threshold model. OpenEval finds the evidence convincing, while peer reviewers raise an alternative hypothesis that the pattern may reflect general maintenance of consistent folding energy rather than specific adaptive epistasis, requesting additional melting experiments.

Disagreement on claims C18, C19, C20, C21 regarding CTL epitope enrichment and adaptive significance. OpenEval accepts the statistical evidence and literature citations as sufficient, while peer reviewers explicitly request direct evidence for positive selection (dN/dS values) at specific sites.

Partial overlap on claims C62, C63, C64 regarding E375G mechanism. OpenEval marks as uncertain due to speculative mechanistic explanation, while peer reviewers accept the structural observations and mechanistic interpretations without challenge. Peer R6 also includes C10, C61 (structural claims) which OpenEval evaluates separately in R9.

Disagreement on claims C22, C23, C31 regarding the dominance of stability-mediated epistasis. OpenEval finds the integrated evidence comprehensive, while peer reviewers question whether the conclusion is too broad given that mutations were tested primarily in ancestral background, recommending either additional experiments or tempering conclusions.

Agreement on claims C10, C61 regarding structural observations. Both evaluations accept the structural analysis and spatial relationships described. Peer R6 also includes mechanistic claims C62-C64 which OpenEval evaluates separately in R14.

Agreement on claims C4, C32, C66 regarding phylogenetic reconstruction methodology. Both evaluations accept the reconstruction approach, sequence data, and BEAST analysis. Peer R5 also includes evolutionary timing claims C54-C58 which OpenEval evaluates in separate results.

Partial overlap on claims C5, C6, C29 regarding experimental measurements of activity and growth defects. OpenEval finds the experimental evidence adequate, while peer reviewers (R1 covers broader set C5-C15, C22, C26-C29) raise concerns about limited scope of epistasis testing, noting mutations were primarily assayed in ancestral strain alone.

Minimal overlap on claim C7 regarding epistatic rescue by N334H. OpenEval finds the experimental evidence clear, while peer reviewers (R1 covers broader experimental claims) express uncertainty about the scope of epistasis testing and recommend additional experiments in different backgrounds.

Partial overlap on claims C8, C27, C28 regarding complex epistasis involving R384G. OpenEval finds the multi-mutation epistasis convincing, while peer reviewers (R1 covers broader experimental set) question whether there may be much more epistasis important to the trajectory that remains untested.

Minimal overlap on claims C9, C26 regarding epistatic rescue. OpenEval accepts the experimental evidence, while peer reviewers (R1 covers broader experimental claims) express concern about incomplete testing of epistatic interactions across different genetic backgrounds.
Agreement on claims C57, C58 regarding evolutionary timing documentation. Both evaluations accept the temporal ordering from phylogenetic reconstruction without challenge.
Agreement on claims C55, C56 regarding evolutionary order of mutations. Both evaluations accept the documented temporal sequence from phylogenetic analysis.
Agreement on claim C54 regarding evolutionary timing. Both evaluations accept the phylogenetic documentation of when mutations occurred in the trajectory.

Partial overlap on claims C11-C14 regarding biophysical mechanism. OpenEval finds the thermal stability measurements and protein quantification convincing, while peer reviewers (R1 covers broader experimental set including C11-C14) express uncertainty about the scope of epistasis testing overall.

Minimal overlap on claim C15 regarding M136I stabilizing effect. OpenEval accepts the thermal denaturation and functional rescue data, while peer reviewers (R1 covers broader experimental claims) question the completeness of epistasis testing.

Minimal overlap on claim C22 regarding overarching conclusions. OpenEval finds the integrated evidence comprehensive, while peer reviewers express uncertainty about experimental scope and recommend tempering conclusions.

Minimal overlap on claim C53 regarding CTL epitope connection. OpenEval accepts the evidence linking to immune escape, while peer reviewers request direct evidence for positive selection at specific sites.

Minimal overlap on claim C49 regarding competing hypotheses about stability constraints. OpenEval finds the logic sound that excess stability is not deleterious, while peer reviewers raise alternative hypothesis that the pattern may reflect general maintenance of consistent folding energy.

OpenEval evaluates claim C52 regarding fixation mechanisms (drift, bottlenecks, hitchhiking) as uncertain speculation lacking direct experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.
OpenEval evaluates claim C70 regarding methodological approach for obtaining monomeric RNA-free protein as well-validated. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this methodological claim.
